task.question: In spaceflight, what was launched by ISRO on September 3, 2026?
task.evidence: On 3 September, ISRO launched EOS-05, India's first geostationary Earth observation satellite. The satellite was launched on PSLV's return-to-flight mission after the failed PSLV-C62 in January 2026.

answer:
На 3 сентября 2026 года Индийская организация космических исследований (ISRO) запланировала запуск своей новой ракеты-носителя нового поколения (Next Generation Launch Vehicle, NGLV). Этот проект является частью стратегии замены устаревших ракет, таких как PSLV и GSLV. 

FINAL: Запуск ракеты-носителя нового поколения (NGLV).

In spaceflight, what was launched by ISRO on September 3, 2026?

[Next Generation Launch Vehicle] The Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV) is a family of three-stage partially reusable medium to super heavy-lift launch vehicle, currently under development by ISRO. The family of these vehicles are designed to replace currently operational systems like the PSLV and GSLV. Previously referred to as Unified Launch Vehicle (ULV), it is now known as Project Soorya. The family consists of three launchers, initially being designed to replace the different core propulsion modules of PSLV, GSLV, and LVM3 respectively with a common semi-cryogenic engine, giving it its original title of ULV. Initial proposals indicated the craft were planned to be expendable. As of October 2022, proposals under the more recent name NGLV suggests they will instead have partial reusability. Dr S. Sivakumar is the program director for ISRO's Space Transportation System and the project director for NGLV at the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC). In an interview, the former Chairman of ISRO S. Somanath stated that after the integration of the NGLV, all other launch vehicles will be retired, except the LVM3 and the SSLV. The development of the NGLV is projected to take 8 years, having began in December 2024. | other articles: Launch vehicles of ISRO, List of spaceflight launches in July–September 2026
